```{=html}
<style>

#panel .btn:hover { background: #18583a; }
#panel .card p.status { color: #555; font-size: 0.85rem; }
#panel .waiting { background: #fff6d6; border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; margin: 0 0 0.5rem; }
#panel .links { font-size: 0.9rem; }
#panel .versions { margin: 0.25rem 0 0; }
#panel .copy { font-size: 0.85rem; padding: 0 0.5rem; border: 1px solid #1f6f43; border-radius: 4px; background: #fff;
               color: #1f6f43; cursor: pointer; }
#panel #latest-export code { font-size: 0.8rem; word-break: break-all; }
#panel .hint { font-size: 0.9rem; background: #eef4fb; border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; }
</style>

<script>
(() => {
  const repo = document.getElementById("panel").dataset.repo;
  const gh = `https://github.com/${repo}`;
  const api = (path) => fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${repo}${path}`).then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : null));
  const link = (href, text) => `<a href="${href}" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">${text}</a>`;
  const waiting = document.getElementById("waiting");
  const notice = (html) => waiting.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", `<p class="waiting">${html}</p>`);

  document.querySelectorAll("[data-workflow]").forEach((a) => { a.href = `${gh}/actions/workflows/${a.dataset.workflow}`; });
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-href]").forEach((a) => { a.href = gh + a.dataset.href; });
  document.querySelectorAll("#panel a").forEach((a) => { a.target = "_blank"; a.rel = "noopener noreferrer"; });

  // Last run of each task.
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-status]").forEach(async (p) => {
    const runs = await api(`/actions/workflows/${p.dataset.status}/runs?per_page=1`);
    const run = runs && runs.workflow_runs[0];
    if (!run) { p.textContent = runs ? "Not run yet." : ""; return; }
    const state = run.status !== "completed" ? "⏳ running" :
      run.conclusion === "success" ? "✅ succeeded" : `❌ ${run.conclusion}`;
    p.innerHTML = `${state}, ${new Date(run.created_at).toLocaleString()} · ${link(run.html_url, "details")}`;
  });

  // Imports waiting for review, and releases prepared but not yet published (notes still say "DOI reserved").
  api("/pulls?state=open&per_page=50").then((pulls) => {
    const imports = (pulls || []).filter((p) => p.head.ref.startsWith("google-doc-import-"));
    if (imports.length) notice(`Import waiting for review (step 1): ${imports.map((p) => link(p.html_url, p.title)).join(", ")}`);
  });
  // Link to the newest Google Doc made by "Export to Google Doc" (written next to this page by that workflow).
  fetch("latest-export.json", { cache: "no-store" }).then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : null)).then((e) => {
    if (!e) return;
    const box = document.getElementById("latest-export");
    box.innerHTML = `Latest Google Doc (export of version ${e.version}, ${e.created}): ${link(e.url, "Open")} · ` +
      `<button type="button" class="copy">Copy link</button><br><code>${e.url}</code>`;
    box.querySelector(".copy").addEventListener("click", (ev) =>
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(e.url).then(() => { ev.target.textContent = "Copied"; }));
  }).catch(() => {});

  // Current versions, from the tags and next_version in the frontmatter (same rules as scripts/versions.py).
  Promise.all([api("/tags?per_page=100"),
               fetch(`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/${repo}/main/IPBES_Data_Vision.qmd`).then((r) => (r.ok ? r.text() : ""))])
  .then(([list, qmd]) => {
    const ts = (list || []).map((t) => t.name.match(/^v(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:-(beta|rc|test)\.(\d+))?$/)).filter(Boolean)
      .map((m) => ({ v: [+m[1], +m[2]], kind: m[3] || null, n: +(m[4] || 0) }));
    const cmp = (a, b) => a[0] - b[0] || a[1] - b[1];
    const highest = (vs, start) => vs.reduce((x, y) => (cmp(y, x) > 0 ? y : x), start);
    const released = highest(ts.filter((t) => !t.kind).map((t) => t.v), [1, 0]);
    const allowed = [[released[0], released[1] + 1], [released[0] + 1, 0]];
    const m = qmd.match(/^next_version:\s*"?v?(\d+)\.(\d+)/m);
    const declared = m ? [+m[1], +m[2]] : null;
    const target = declared && allowed.some((a) => cmp(a, declared) === 0) ? declared : allowed[0];
    const last = (kind) => Math.max(0, ...ts.filter((t) => t.kind === kind && cmp(t.v, target) === 0).map((t) => t.n));
    const v = (x) => x.join(".");
    document.getElementById("versions").innerHTML = `Latest release: <b>${v(released)}</b> · Working towards <b>${v(target)}</b>` +
      (last("rc") ? ` · latest pre-release ${v(target)}-rc.${last("rc")}` : " · no pre-release yet") +
      (last("beta") ? ` · latest accepted change ${v(target)}-beta.${last("beta")}` : "");
  });

  api("/releases?per_page=20").then((releases) => {
    const pending = (releases || []).filter((r) => !r.prerelease && /^DOI reserved:/m.test(r.body || ""));
    if (pending.length) notice(`Release ready to publish (step 4): ${pending.map((r) => link(r.html_url, r.tag_name)).join(", ")}`);
  });
})();
</script>
```

You need to be signed in to GitHub with an account that may edit this repository. Each task takes a few minutes; its status appears above (reload the page).

## What the buttons do

1. **Import from Google Doc** copies the text and the bibliographic tables from the Google Doc. Nothing changes on the website yet: you get a page showing every change, where you accept (**Merge**) or discard (**Close**) it. An accepted import gets the next beta number. The imported Doc gets a highlighted line at the top, "IMPORTED on … into <link to the review page>", and is locked (read-only). The form takes a Doc link; leave it empty to import the latest exported Doc (shown above the buttons).
2. **Export to Google Doc** asks which version this round of editing prepares (e.g. `1.1` for a minor or `2.0` for a major change; empty keeps the current one) and creates a **new** Google Doc in your Drive with the current text and the bibliographic tables, including that version; its link is shown under the run's *details*. The previous export gets a highlighted line at the top, "NEW VERSION AVAILABLE … Continue in: <link>", is locked (read-only) and is moved into a folder `archive` next to it (its link stays the same); otherwise existing Docs are not changed. Paste the new Doc's link into the import form later (or ask the technical admin to make it the usual Doc).
3. **Make a release or pre-release** asks for the type and what changed (items separated by `;`). There is no version number to type: it follows the rules below.
   - **Pre-release**: the next release candidate, e.g. `1.1-rc.2`. No DOI, archived on GitHub, shown at the *Pre-release preview* link.
   - **Release**: the latest release candidate, unchanged, becomes the final version, e.g. `1.1-rc.2` → `1.1`. A DOI is reserved and a Zenodo draft prepared, but nothing is public until step 4. If the text changed after that candidate, make a new pre-release first.
4. **Publish release**: after a release in step 3, check the Zenodo draft and the PDF, then publish. This makes the DOI permanent and updates the website. Leave the form empty to publish the newest release.

This panel is always at <https://ipbes-data.github.io/IPBES_Data_Vision/admin/> and is updated whenever the repository changes.

## Version rules

Released versions are `MAJOR.MINOR` (`1.0`, `1.1`, `2.0`); work in progress carries a suffix (`1.1-beta.3`, `1.1-rc.2`). A *cycle* is the work between two releases; the line above the buttons shows the current one.

| Step | Version |
|---|---|
| Import (or other change to the text) accepted | next **beta**, e.g. `1.1-beta.3`: only recorded, no PDF, no DOI |
| Export | asks for the version being prepared (`1.1` or `2.0`), which goes into the Doc's *Version* row; the Doc also shows "Based on version …" |
| Pre-release | next **release candidate**, e.g. `1.1-rc.2`: PDF on GitHub, preview site, no DOI |
| Release + Publish | the latest release candidate **unchanged** becomes `1.1`, with a DOI |

- **Minor or major is decided at export**: you type only the `MAJOR.MINOR` part, and it must be the next minor (`1.0 → 1.1`) or the next major (`1.0 → 2.0`) version. It is written into the Google Doc's *Version* row, can be corrected there, and takes effect when the import is accepted. The `-beta.N` / `-rc.N` part is always added automatically. Until a version is chosen, the next minor is assumed.
- **Which one?**
  - **Minor** (`1.0 → 1.1`): the same content, better expressed or updated — wording, clarifications, corrections, updated references or names, changes to editors, contact or publisher.
  - **Major** (`1.0 → 2.0`): what the Vision says or commits to changes — aims, tracks or targets (including their dates) added, removed or substantially changed, the document restructured, or changes following a new Plenary decision. Rule of thumb: would someone citing the previous version need to know that the substance changed?
- Beta and release-candidate numbers start at 1 for each new version; betas keep counting after a release candidate.
- A release always publishes a release candidate exactly as it was reviewed; if the text changed since, make a new pre-release first. Released numbers only go up.
- While `ZENODO_TARGET` is `sandbox`, releases are test releases tagged `1.1-test.N`; they are not versions and do not end the cycle.
- The numbers are git tags (`v1.1-beta.3`, …), handed out by `scripts/versions.py`.

## Versions step by step: the example of 2.0

This walks through one full cycle, using what has actually happened so far with version 2.0 and what comes next.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  R1["Released: 1.0<br/>(on Zenodo)"] --> E["1. Export to Google Doc<br/>choose target: 1.1 (minor) or 2.0 (major)"]
  E --> D["Edit in the Google Doc"]
  D --> I["2. Import from Google Doc<br/>review page: Merge"]
  I --> B["beta: 2.0-beta.N<br/>(automatic, not published)"]
  B -->|more edits| D
  B --> P["3. Pre-release<br/>release candidate 2.0-rc.N<br/>PDF + /preview/, no DOI"]
  P -->|changes needed| D
  P --> RL["4. Release<br/>2.0-rc.N becomes 2.0<br/>DOI reserved, Zenodo draft"]
  RL --> PB["5. Publish release<br/>DOI minted, website shows 2.0"]
  PB --> E2["Next export: target 2.1 or 3.0<br/>next betas: 2.1-beta.1, ..."]
```

### Where 2.0 stands now

| When | What happened | Version |
|---|---|---|
| 25 April 2022 | Published on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5513474) | **1.0** (latest release) |
| 29 October 2026 | Exported to Google Docs with *Target version* **2.0** (a major change: new aims, tracks and targets) | target 2.0 |
| 29 October 2026 | Changes accepted into the repository (version rules, website layout, Google Docs sync) | 2.0-beta.1 to 2.0-beta.4 |
| 29 October 2026 | 2.0-beta.1 published for review at the *Pre-release* button (a one-off; normally step 3 publishes a release candidate) | 2.0-beta.1 (published) |

The line above the buttons always shows the current state, e.g. *Latest release: 1.0 · Working towards 2.0 · latest accepted change 2.0-beta.4*.

### 1. Start a round of editing and decide minor or major

Click **Export to Google Doc**. The form asks for the **Target version**: only `MAJOR.MINOR`, and only the next minor or the next major of the latest release. After 1.0 that is `1.1` or `2.0`; after 2.0 it will be `2.1` or `3.0`. Leave it empty to keep the current target.

- **Minor** (`1.0 → 1.1`): the same content, better expressed or updated — wording, corrections, references, editors.
- **Major** (`1.0 → 2.0`): what the Vision says or commits to changes — aims, tracks or targets added, removed or substantially changed, a new structure, a new Plenary decision.

The new Google Doc shows *Current version* (e.g. `2.0-beta.4`, for information) and *Target version* (`2.0`) in its *Document information* table. The target can still be corrected there before importing. The previous export is marked "NEW VERSION AVAILABLE", locked and moved into the folder `archive`.

### 2. Bring edits back: a beta

When the editing round is done, click **Import from Google Doc** (form empty = the latest exported Doc). You get a review page listing every change; click **Merge** to accept, **Close** to discard. The Doc is marked "IMPORTED" and locked.

Accepting gives the text the **next beta number automatically**: the next import after 2.0-beta.4 becomes **2.0-beta.5**. Betas are only recorded: no PDF, no website, no DOI. Changes to the page layout in the repository also count as betas (that is how 2.0-beta.2 to 2.0-beta.4 came about). Repeat export → edit → import as often as needed; the target stays 2.0.

### 3. Publish for review: a release candidate

When the text is ready for review, click **Make a release or pre-release**, choose **Pre-release (for review, no DOI)** and write what changed (items separated by `;`). The text becomes the next **release candidate**: the first one for 2.0 is **2.0-rc.1**.

- The PDF and release notes appear as a GitHub pre-release, the website version at the **Pre-release** button (`/preview/`), with the amber banner "for review, not for citation".
- If the review asks for changes: edit, export/import as in steps 1–2 (giving 2.0-beta.6, …), then make another pre-release: **2.0-rc.2**.
- A pre-release is refused if nothing has changed since the last one.

### 4. Release: the reviewed candidate gets the final number

When the task force approves the latest release candidate, click **Make a release or pre-release** and choose **Release (citable, with DOI)**. There is no version to type: the latest candidate becomes the final version, **2.0-rc.2 → 2.0**, exactly as reviewed.

- Refused if the text changed after that candidate ("make a new pre-release first"), so the DOI always belongs to a reviewed text.
- A DOI is reserved on Zenodo and a Zenodo draft is filled (PDF, title, version, date, editors, release notes; access *closed* for now). The GitHub release shows "DOI reserved: …". **Nothing public changes yet.**
- While `ZENODO_TARGET` is `sandbox`, this makes a test release `2.0-test.N` on the Zenodo sandbox instead; it is not a version.

### 5. Publish: the DOI becomes permanent

Check the Zenodo draft (link in the run's details) and the PDF on the GitHub release. If both are right, click **Publish release** (form empty = the release waiting to be published).

- The DOI is minted on Zenodo and added to the release notes.
- The website shows **2.0** with the green banner "Version 2.0 · released … · cite it with DOI …"; 1.0 stays available at *All versions*.
- The preview is removed (its candidate is now the release); the *Pre-release* button disappears until the next pre-release.

If the draft is wrong instead: delete the draft on Zenodo and the release and its tag on GitHub, fix the text, and continue from step 3.

### 6. The next cycle

After 2.0 is published, the next export offers **2.1** (minor) or **3.0** (major). Accepted edits then count as **2.1-beta.1**, **2.1-beta.2**, …, the first pre-release becomes **2.1-rc.1**, and its release **2.1**. Beta and release-candidate numbers always start again at 1 for each new version.

## One-time setup (for the technical admin)

### GitHub

*Settings → Actions → General*: under *Workflow permissions* tick **Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests** (needed by the import). GitHub Pages must serve the `gh-pages` branch.

*Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions*:

| Name | Kind | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `ZENODO_TARGET` | variable | `sandbox` (tests) or `production` (real DOIs) |
| `ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN` | secret | sandbox.zenodo.org token with `deposit:write` and `deposit:actions` |
| `ZENODO_TOKEN` | secret | zenodo.org token with `deposit:write` and `deposit:actions` |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH` | secret | Google sign-in, created by `scripts/gdoc.py login` (see below) |
| `GDOC_ID` | variable | link or ID of the usual Google Doc to import from |
| `GDRIVE_FOLDER_ID` | variable | optional: link or ID of the Drive folder for exports (default: My Drive) |

People who use the panel need *Write* access to the repository.

### Google (works with a free Google account)

Import and export act as **one Google account** (yours, or a dedicated one): they can read every Doc that account can open, and exports are new Docs owned by it, using its normal Drive storage. Set up once, on a computer with Python:

1. In the [Google Cloud console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), signed in with that account, create a project and enable the **Google Drive API** and the **Google Docs API** (the Docs API writes the "new version" and "imported" notices). No billing is needed.
2. *Google Auth Platform → Branding* (German: *Branding*): app name (e.g. "IPBES Vision"), support e-mail and developer contact e-mail, plus — required for publishing — **App home page** `https://ipbes-data.github.io/IPBES_Data_Vision/admin/`, **Privacy policy link** `https://ipbes-data.github.io/IPBES_Data_Vision/admin/#privacy` and **Authorized domain** `ipbes-data.github.io`; save. Then *Audience* (*Zielgruppe*): user type **External**, then **Publish app** (*App veröffentlichen*); the status must read "In production" (*In Produktion*). In "Testing" status only listed test users can sign in, and Google ends the sign-in after 7 days.
3. *Clients → Create client*, type **Desktop app**; download the JSON file (e.g. `client.json`).
4. In this repository run, with the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) signed in:

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/gdoc.py login client.json | gh secret set GOOGLE_OAUTH
   ```

   A browser opens; sign in with the Google account. Google warns that the app is not verified: choose *Advanced → Go to IPBES Vision sync* (it is your own app) and allow access to Google Drive. Then delete `client.json`.

If an import or export later fails with "sign-in has expired or was revoked" (e.g. after removing the app's access in the Google account, or after 6 months without use), repeat step 4.

### How the Google Doc must be laid out

Everything before the first heading is the front matter; the text of the Vision starts at the first **Heading 1**.

- **Document information** table, two columns, one row per field: `Title`, `Produced by`, `Publisher`, `Contact e-mail`, `Current version (information only)`, `Target version`. All but *Current version* are required and imported; only the second column is edited. *Current version* is the version of the text in the Doc (e.g. `2.0-beta.3`); *Target version* is what the edits work towards (`MAJOR.MINOR`, e.g. `2.0`).
- **Editors** table with the columns `Name | Institution | ORCID`, one row per editor; add or delete rows as needed. Institution and ORCID may be empty; an ORCID may be given as number or as orcid.org link.
- Anything else before the first heading (notes, Google's table of contents) is ignored.
- Section titles use **Heading 1** (sub-sections Heading 2, …). Typed numbers such as "I." or "2.1" in headings are removed; the website and PDF number sections themselves.
- Suggestions must be accepted or rejected before importing; comments are not imported.

If a table is missing or a value is invalid, the import stops without changing anything and lists what to fix (shown under the failed run's *details*).

An export writes exactly this layout, so the easiest start is to run **Export to Google Doc** once and edit the new Doc.

### Zenodo

`ZENODO_TARGET` selects the Zenodo used by releases. The concept DOIs ("all versions" DOI) are in the frontmatter of `IPBES_Data_Vision.qmd` (`zenodo.concept_doi`, `zenodo.sandbox_concept_doi`). Sandbox releases never change the official website. If a prepared release is wrong, delete the draft on Zenodo and the release and its tag on GitHub, then make it again.

### Without the panel

```bash
make preview                                                    # live preview while editing
make build                                                      # website + PDF as unreleased draft
python3 scripts/release.py prepare --version 1.2 --prerelease   # pre-release build, no Zenodo
export GOOGLE_OAUTH="$(python3 scripts/gdoc.py login client.json)"   # sign in once per shell
python3 scripts/gdoc.py import <doc link>
```

## Privacy: Google sign-in "IPBES Vision" {#privacy}

The Google sign-in "IPBES Vision" is used only by the automated tasks of this repository (*Import from Google Doc*, *Export to Google Doc*) to move the text of the IPBES Data Management Vision between this repository and Google Docs in the Google Drive of the account that signed in.

- **What is accessed:** the import opens only the Google Doc it is given and reads its content; the export creates a new Google Doc. No other files are opened, changed or deleted.
- **What is stored:** the imported text and bibliographic information are stored in this public repository, because they are the content of the Vision. Nothing else from Google, and no personal data of Google users, is stored, shared or sold.
- **Where the sign-in is kept:** as an encrypted secret of this GitHub repository, used only by these tasks.
- **Withdrawing access:** at any time at <https://myaccount.google.com/permissions> (remove "IPBES Vision"); import and export then stop working until someone signs in again.
- **Contact:** IPBES.Vision@krugs.de
